eras.name: Kamarupa period
eras.label: 350–1100 CE
eras.blurb: The Varman, Salastambha and Pala dynasties of ancient Kamarupa, ruling most of the Brahmaputra valley.

eras.name: Western (Namoni) Assam after 1100
eras.label: 1100–1826, Koch lines to 1949
eras.blurb: The kingdoms of Lower (Namoni) Assam and north Bengal after the Palas: the successors of Kamarupa, Kamata, the Khen and Bhuyan rulers, and the Koch kingdom with its branches Koch Hajo, Koch Bihar, Darrang, Beltola, Bijni and Khaspur. Sultans from Bengal and Delhi raided this region from 1206.

eras.name: Ahom period
eras.blurb: The Tai-Ahom kingdom of Upper (Ujoni) Assam, founded by Sukaphaa in 1228 and ended by the Burmese invasions and the Treaty of Yandabo in 1826: its kings, queens, nobles and rebels, and the foreign commanders they fought.

eras.name: Neighbouring kingdoms
eras.label: c. 1300–1830
eras.blurb: The Chutia kingdom of Sadiya, the Dimasa (Kachari) and Barahi kingdoms of the centre and south, and Jaintia and Manipur on the edge of the hills.

eras.name: Saints, poets and writers
eras.label: 13th–17th century
eras.blurb: Assamese literature and the bhakti movement, which grew across the Kamata, Koch and Ahom lands.

characters.name: Xuanzang
characters.label: 602–664 CE (visited 643)
characters.summary: Buddhist monk whose account of his 643 visit is a key outside description of Kamarupa.

characters.name: Prithu
characters.label: c. 1187–1228 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Ruler of Kamarupa remembered for destroying Bakhtiyar Khalji's army in 1205–06 and for resisting Iwaz Khalji in 1226–28; one account says he was killed in a plot in 1228. Whether the Prithu of Juzjani's chronicle is this king is disputed.
characters.notes: One list dates him 1187–1228 with a capital at Bhittargarh. Some scholars treat “Prithu” as a rebel in Awadh and credit the Kamarupa resistance to other rulers. One source suggests the name Viswasundaradeva.

characters.name: Chaolung Sukaphaa
characters.summary: Born around 1189 in Mong Mao, he left in 1215, crossed the Patkai hills and reached Namrup in December 1228, founding the Ahom kingdom that lasted until 1826. He built Charaideo in 1253.
characters.notes: Married daughters of the Moran chief Badaucha and the Barahi chief Thakumatha. Moved his base from 1236 (Mungklang) through Habung (1240) and Ligirigaon (1244) before Charaideo.

characters.name: Suteuphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sukaphaa; died a natural death.
characters.notes: Catalogued scenes cover the Dikhou frontier with the Kacharis and the Naga hill campaigns.

characters.name: Sudangphaa (Bamuni Konwar)
characters.summary: Son of Tyao Khamti, raised by a Brahmin family in Habung after his mother's execution; found and enthroned at about fifteen in 1397. He introduced the Singarigharutha coronation (1403) and let Hindu rites into the court.
characters.notes: Peace treaty fixing the Patkai boundary in 1401; capital moved to Charguwa in 1403.

characters.name: Durlabhnarayan (Kamata)
characters.label: c. 1330–1350 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Son of Pratapdhwaj who took Kamrup, Goalpara and Koch Bihar from Kamatapur. His court poets produced early Assamese literature, including Hema Saraswati and Harihara Vipra.
characters.notes: Replaces the earlier early-14th-century guess. The catalogue ties him to the Ahom–Kamata war of c. 1324, which falls in Pratapdhwaj's reign by these dates. The chronology and extent of his rule are disputed.

characters.name: Suhungmung (Swarganarayan)
characters.summary: Expanded the kingdom for the first time since Sukaphaa, annexing Chutia and Dimasa territory and repelling the Bengal invasions of 1527 and 1532–33. First Ahom king to take a Hindu title, Swarganarayan.
characters.notes: Annexed Habung 1512; Chutia kingdom 1523–24; created the Borpatragohain post 1527; killed in his sleep in 1539 by his servant Ratiman.

characters.name: Biswa Singha
characters.label: r. 1515–1540
characters.summary: Son of Hariya Mandal and Hira. Defeated the Baro-Bhuyans and founded the Koch kingdom in Kamata; his sons Nara Narayan and Chilarai followed.
characters.notes: Campaigns began c. 1509; coronation 1515. Sources differ on the cause of death.

characters.name: Nara Narayan
characters.label: r. 1540–1587
characters.summary: Took the Koch kingdom to its peak with his brother Chilarai as commander. Introduced the Narayani silver coin; Sankardev's teaching spread in his time.
characters.notes: Infobox gives 1554–1587; text gives 1540. Died 1587 (some sources 1588).

characters.name: Chilarai (Sukladhwaj)
characters.summary: Third son of Biswa Singha and commander-in-chief under Nara Narayan. Led the 1562–63 invasion that forced the Treaty of Majuli; died of smallpox in 1571.
characters.notes: Spouse: Kamalpriya.

characters.name: Srimanta Sankardev
characters.label: 1449–1568 (traditional)
characters.summary: Founder of the Ekasarana bhakti movement and a defining figure of Assamese literature, music and dance. Wrote the Kirtana-ghosha, borgeets and Ankia Naat plays.
characters.notes: Scholars give his death as 1569. Wives: Suryava and Kalindi; son Ramananda.

characters.name: Madhavdev
characters.summary: Sankardev's chief disciple and successor, converted after a debate around 1532. Wrote the Naam Ghosa and about 191 borgeets.

characters.name: Momai Tamuli Borbarua
characters.label: c. 1590–1663 (sources vary)
characters.summary: Rose from humble origins to become the first Borbarua. Systematised the paik system in 1609, commanded at Duimunsila (1638) and signed the Treaty of Asurar Ali (1639). Father of Lachit Borphukan.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1664 and a category gives 1650 for his death.

characters.name: Sati Sadhani
characters.label: 16th century (legend)
characters.summary: Heroine of an Assamese folk legend of devotion and courage.
characters.notes: Legendary figure with no verified dates.

characters.name: Pratap Singha (Susenghphaa)
characters.summary: Created the Borbarua and Borphukan offices, reorganised the paik system through Momai Tamuli Borbarua, and fought the first Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Also known as Burha Roja and Buddhiswarganarayan. Married Mangaldahi, daughter of Parikshit Narayan, in 1608.

characters.name: Atan Burhagohain
characters.label: Burhagohain 1662–1679
characters.summary: Appointed Burhagohain in January 1662 while Mir Jumla held Garhgaon. Negotiated the Treaty of Ghilajharighat, commanded the northern division at Saraighat and twice declined the crown. Murdered in 1679 by men of Laluk Sola Borphukan.
characters.notes: Served under eight kings.

characters.name: Jayadhwaj Singha (Sutamla)
characters.summary: Drove the Mughals from Guwahati in 1648. Mir Jumla took Garhgaon in March 1662; the king withdrew to Namrup and signed the Treaty of Ghilajharighat in January 1663. A patron of Vaishnava satras.
characters.notes: Called Bhagania Roja (“the fugitive”). Struck the first coins in his name.

characters.name: Mir Jumla
characters.summary: Invaded Assam in January 1662, took Garhgaon in March and agreed the Treaty of Ghilajharighat in January 1663. Died on the return at Mankachar on 30 March 1663.
characters.notes: Born in Isfahan in 1591.

characters.name: Chakradhwaj Singha (Supangmung)
characters.summary: Refused Mughal tribute, rebuilt the army and recaptured Guwahati in 1667. Appointed Atan Burhagohain Rajmantri Dangaria and Lachit Borphukan commander.
characters.notes: Died April 1670.

characters.name: Lachit Borphukan
characters.summary: Retook Guwahati in 1667 and led the Ahom victory over a larger Mughal fleet at Saraighat in 1671. Died the next year, and his remains lie in a maidam at Jorhat.
characters.notes: Born 24 November 1622; died 25 April 1672 at Kaliabor. Fought at Alaboi in 1669.

characters.name: Joymoti Konwari
characters.label: d. 1680
characters.role: Ahom princess and wife of Gadadhar Singha
characters.summary: Wife of the prince who became king Gadadhar Singha. Tortured and killed by agents of Sulikphaa and Laluk Sola Borphukan while her husband hid in exile.

characters.name: Gadadhar Singha (Supaatphaa)
characters.summary: Founder of the Tungkhungia line. Came out of exile in the Naga hills to take the throne in 1681 and retook Guwahati at Itakhuli in 1682, ending the Ahom–Mughal wars.
characters.notes: Husband of Joymoti Konwari. Built the Dhodar Ali road and began a land survey.
characters.relation: Son of Gobar Roja; first Tungkhungia king

characters.name: Rudra Singha (Sukhrungphaa)
characters.summary: Took the kingdom to its peak, founded Rangpur as the capital, campaigned against the Dimasa and Jaintia kingdoms (1706–08) and planned a great war on Mughal Bengal, dying before it began.
characters.notes: Born c. 1665; died 27 August 1714 at North Guwahati.

characters.name: Siva Singha (Sutanphaa)
characters.summary: A devout Shakta who gave land to temples and Brahmins and shared royal authority with his queens, who ruled in turn as Bar Raja. A golden age of Assamese manuscripts.

characters.name: Phuleswari (Pramatheswari)
characters.label: Bar Raja 1722–1731
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: A dancer of the Nat caste made Bar Raja under Siva Singha after astrologers predicted the king's fall. Minted coins in joint names and pressed to make Shaktism the state religion; died in 1731 in childbirth.
characters.notes: Her insult to the Moamoria Gosains is cited as a cause of the later rebellion.

characters.name: Pramatta Singha (Sunenphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Siva Singha; died naturally. Catalogued scenes show Rang Ghar games in his reign.

characters.name: Kamaleswar Singha (Suklingphaa)
characters.summary: Placed on the throne as an infant by Purnananda Burhagohain, who held real power; died of smallpox.

characters.name: Chandrakanta Singha (Sudingphaa)
characters.summary: Named king at about fourteen by Purnananda Burhagohain. Deposed in 1818, reinstalled by the Burmese in 1819, defeated in 1822 and fled to British territory. Died in Guwahati in 1839.
characters.notes: Born c. 1797. After Yandabo he received a pension of 500 rupees.

characters.name: Purnananda Burhagohain
characters.label: d. 27 March 1817
characters.summary: Placed Kamaleswar and then Chandrakanta on the throne and ran the state for two decades. Collapsed and died on 27 March 1817 on learning that Badan Chandra Borphukan was with the Burmese.
characters.notes: His eldest son Ruchinath succeeded him as Burhagohain.

characters.name: Badan Chandra Borphukan
characters.label: d. 1817–1818
characters.summary: Went to the Burmese court in 1816 seeking help against Purnananda Burhagohain and returned with an army in 1817. Assassinated by Subedar Rup Singh.
characters.notes: Sources give 1817 or 1818 for the assassination; the Wikipedia article gives 1818.

characters.name: Piyali Phukan
characters.label: d. 1830
characters.summary: Ahom noble who plotted against the East India Company and was executed in 1830.

characters.name: Maniram Dewan
characters.summary: Assamese entrepreneur who pioneered tea planting and was hanged for his part in the 1857 revolt.

characters.name: Anandaram Dhekial Phukan
characters.summary: Early Assamese reformer who pressed for the Assamese language in schools and courts.

characters.name: Hemchandra Baruah
characters.summary: Compiled the first major Assamese dictionary, Hemkosh, and a grammar.

characters.name: Gunabhiram Baruah
characters.summary: Wrote the first Assamese biography and a history of Assam; a social reformer.

characters.name: Nathan Brown
characters.summary: Missionary and printer who helped establish Assamese in print in the 1830s.

characters.name: Miles Bronson
characters.summary: Missionary who compiled an Assamese–English dictionary.

characters.name: Lakshminath Bezbaroa
characters.summary: Pioneering writer and satirist who shaped modern Assamese literature.

characters.name: Padmanath Gohain Baruah
characters.summary: Playwright and historian who wrote on Assamese literature and the Ahom period.

characters.name: Hemchandra Goswami
characters.summary: Scholar known for cataloguing old Assamese manuscripts.

characters.name: Bhogeswari Phukanani
characters.label: c. 1885–1942
characters.summary: Veteran of the Quit India movement, killed at Behali in 1942.

characters.name: Kanaklata Barua
characters.summary: Young Quit India martyr shot while leading a procession to Gohpur police station.

characters.name: Kushal Konwar
characters.summary: Executed by the British in 1943 for the Sarupathar derailment.

characters.name: Gopinath Bordoloi
characters.summary: Led Assam's Congress ministry from 1946 and resisted its grouping into Pakistan.

characters.name: Jyotiprasad Agarwala
characters.summary: Made Assam's first feature film, Joymoti, in 1935; composed the Rupkonwar songs.

characters.name: Bishnu Prasad Rabha
characters.summary: Multi-talented cultural figure known as Kalaguru and a leader of the Left.

characters.name: Chandraprabha Saikiani
characters.summary: Pioneer of women's education and organising in Assam.

characters.name: Bishnuram Medhi
characters.label: 1888–1981 (CM 1950–1957)
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam from 1950 to 1957.

characters.name: Bimala Prasad Chaliha
characters.label: 1912–1971 (CM 1957–1970)
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam from 1957 to 1970.

characters.name: Fakhruddin Ali Ahmed
characters.summary: Assam politician who became the fifth President of India in 1974.

characters.name: Bhupen Hazarika
characters.summary: Singer and composer whose songs made Assam's culture known across India.

characters.name: Hiteswar Saikia
characters.label: 1934–1996 (CM 1983–1985, 1991–1996)
characters.summary: Twice Chief Minister of Assam.

characters.name: Prafulla Kumar Mahanta
characters.label: b. 1952 (CM 1985–1990, 1996–2001)
characters.summary: Student leader of the Assam Movement who became Chief Minister at 33.

characters.name: Tarun Gogoi
characters.label: 1934–2020 (CM 2001–2016)
characters.summary: Chief Minister of Assam for three terms from 2001 to 2016, the longest in the state's history.

characters.name: Pushya Varman
characters.label: 350–374 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 350–374 CE.
characters.notes: Founder; Allahabad Prasasti pillar

characters.name: Samudra Varman
characters.label: 374–398 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 374–398 CE.

characters.name: Bala Varman
characters.label: 398–422 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 398–422 CE.
characters.notes: Father of Amritaprabha, who married Meghavahana of Kashmir; Amritaprabha took Buddhist monk Stunpa with her

characters.name: Kalyan Varman
characters.label: 422–446 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 422–446 CE.
characters.notes: Expanded territory into the Kapili valley; sent a diplomatic mission to China

characters.name: Ganapati Varman
characters.label: 446–470 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 446–470 CE.

characters.name: Mahendra Varman
characters.label: 470–494 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 470–494 CE.
characters.notes: Kumaragupta; Skandagupta; Aswamedh jagya

characters.name: Narayana Varman
characters.label: 494–518 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 494–518 CE.

characters.name: Bhuti Varman
characters.label: 518–542 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 518–542 CE.
characters.notes: Won over Pundravardhana; Badaganga epigraph

characters.name: Chandramukha
characters.label: 542–566 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 542–566 CE.

characters.name: Sthita Varman
characters.label: 566–590 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 566–590 CE.

characters.name: Susthita Varman
characters.label: 590–595 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 590–595 CE.
characters.notes: Mriganka; lost north Bengal to Gupta

characters.name: Supratisthita Varman
characters.label: 595–600 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 595–600 CE.
characters.notes: Brother of Bhaskar Varman

characters.name: Bhaskar Varman
characters.label: 600–650 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Barman dynasty, 600–650 CE.
characters.notes: Ascended throne around 594 AD; alliance with Harshavardhana; campaign against Sasanka leading to capture of Gauda and Karnasuvarna; issued Nidhanpur grants reconfirming Bhutivarman land grants in Pundravardhana; hosted Chinese pilgrim Hiuen Tsang in 642–643 AD; mentioned as Kumararaja in Chinese sources

characters.name: Salastamba
characters.label: 650–670 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 650–670 CE.
characters.notes: Pragjyotishpur to Tezpur or Haruppeswara / Hatakeswara

characters.name: Vijaya / Vigrahastambha
characters.label: Reign dates not given in the source
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, reign dates not given in the source.

characters.name: Palaka
characters.label: Reign dates not given in the source
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, reign dates not given in the source.

characters.name: Kumara
characters.label: Reign dates not given in the source
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, reign dates not given in the source.

characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, reign dates not given in the source.

characters.label: Reign dates not given in the source
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, reign dates not given in the source.

characters.name: Harshadeva (alias Harshavarman)
characters.label: 725–745 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 725–745 CE.
characters.notes: Gaudradi-Kalinga-Kosala-pati (Pasupati epigraph); Nepal Lichvi king Jayadeva-II; Rashtrakuta king Dantidurga (Samangad epigraph)

characters.name: Harjaravarman
characters.label: 815–832 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 815–832 CE.
characters.notes: Hayunthal grant; Tezpur Rock epigraph

characters.name: Vanamalavarmadeva
characters.label: 832–855 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 832–855 CE.
characters.notes: Fasted unto death, evidently under the influence of religion

characters.name: Jayamala / Virabahu
characters.label: 855–860 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 855–860 CE.
characters.notes: Virabahu; he considered the world vain and man’s life a water-drop

characters.name: Balavarman III
characters.label: 860–880 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 860–880 CE.

characters.name: Tyagasimha
characters.label: 890–900 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Salastambha dynasty, 890–900 CE.
characters.notes: Brahmapala was his administrator

characters.name: Brahma Pala
characters.label: 900–920 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 900–920 CE.
characters.notes: Administrator in Salastambha and became founder of Varman dynasty

characters.name: Ratna Pala
characters.label: 920–960 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 920–960 CE.
characters.notes: Choratbari grant; Bargaon grant; Sualkuchi grant; fortified Hadapyaka (Tezpur) and renamed it Durjaya; defeated Gauda king Rajyapala

characters.name: Indra Pala
characters.label: 960–990 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 960–990 CE.
characters.notes: Guwahati grant; Guwa kuchi grant; marital relation to Rashtrakuta; held sway over Pundravardhana

characters.name: Gopala Varman
characters.label: 990–1015 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 990–1015 CE.
characters.notes: His mother was a Rashtrakuta princess named Rajyadevi

characters.name: Harsha Pala
characters.label: 1015–1035 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 1015–1035 CE.
characters.notes: Jatavarman, king of East Bengal, snatched away a part of Pundravardhana

characters.name: Dharma Pala
characters.label: 1035–1060 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 1035–1060 CE.
characters.notes: Khonamukhi grant; Subhankarapataka grant; Pushpabhadra grant

characters.name: Jaya Pala
characters.label: 1075–1100 CE
characters.summary: Ruler of the Pala dynasty, 1075–1100 CE.
characters.notes: Defeated by king Ramapala of Bengal; mentioned in Ramacharita by Sandhyakara Nandi; Ramapala apparently took only possessions in North Bengal and appointed Tingyadeva as ruler

characters.name: Avantivarman
characters.label: c. 650–655 CE
characters.summary: Named in some lists as the last ruler of the Varman line after Bhaskarvarman; his parentage is unknown. This is the row marked “Unknown” in the source CSV.
characters.notes: Sources disagree on the end of the dynasty (650 or 655 CE).

characters.name: Ikhtiyar al-Din Muhammad bin Bakhtiyar Khalji
characters.label: d. 1206
characters.summary: Conquered Bengal and led a failed expedition towards Tibet through Kamarupa in 1206; the retreat ended in disaster.
characters.notes: Some accounts date an earlier attempt to 1203. The identity of the Kamarupa ruler who resisted him is disputed.

characters.name: Sandhya (Kamateswar)
characters.label: c. 1228–1260 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Founder of the Kamata kingdom. Took the throne in 1228 as a vassal of Delhi, then stopped paying tribute; captured and executed Yuzbak in 1257 and moved the capital from Kamarupanagara to Kamatapur after that.
characters.notes: Heritage University paper gives 1228–1265. Control over lands east of the Manas was loose. The reorganisation into the Kamata state is dated c. 1250–1270.

characters.name: Malik Ikhtiyaruddin Yuzbak Tughril Khan
characters.label: d. 1257
characters.summary: Invaded Kamarupa in 1257, won early successes and was then defeated by the Kamata ruler.
characters.notes: Accounts differ on whether he was captured or killed.

characters.name: Sindhu Rai
characters.label: c. 1260/65–1285 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Early Kamata ruler listed between Sandhya and Rup Narayan; no dates or events are given.
characters.notes: Dated 1265–1285 in the Heritage University paper; no events are given.

characters.name: Rup Narayan
characters.label: c. 1285–1300 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Early Kamata ruler; no dates or events are given.
characters.notes: Dated 1285–1300 in the Heritage University paper.

characters.name: Singhadhwaj
characters.label: c. 1300–1305 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Said to have founded a new ruling line by killing the Kameswar of Sandhya's line; his minister Pratapdhwaj later took power.
characters.notes: Dated 1300–1305 in the Heritage University paper.

characters.name: Pratapdhwaj
characters.label: c. 1305–1325 (reconstructed)
characters.role: King of Kamata (minister who took the throne)
characters.summary: Minister of Singhadhwaj who took the throne. Faced Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah's raid in 1321–22 with little success, and his reign overlaps the Ahom–Kamata war of about 1324.
characters.notes: Father of Durlabhnarayan. Dates 1305–1325 appear in two king lists.

characters.name: Dharmanarayan
characters.label: c. 1325–1330 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Cousin of Pratapdhwaj who took power at his death; after a settlement with Durlabhnarayan he kept Rangpur and Mymensingh.
characters.notes: Dated 1325–1330 in one list and 1330–1350 in another that seems to conflate him with Durlabhnarayan.

characters.name: Subinphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suteuphaa; set up the Satghariya Ahom group and died naturally.

characters.name: Sukhaangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Subinphaa. His long war with the Kamata king (from about 1324) ended in a truce sealed by marrying the Kamata princesses Rajani and Bhajani.
characters.notes: The king list gives a natural death, but a footnote says he was deposed and executed.
characters.fate: Natural death (a footnote says deposed and executed)

characters.name: Sukhrangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sukhaangphaa; created the post of Charing Raja. His death was followed by an interregnum (1364–1369).

characters.name: Sutuphaa
characters.summary: Brother of Sukhrangphaa; assassinated. Another interregnum (1376–1380) followed.

characters.name: Tyao Khamti
characters.summary: Brother of Sutuphaa; assassinated by nobles in 1389 (a family tree gives 1387). He led an unsuccessful expedition against the Chutias.
characters.notes: Followed by an interregnum until 1397.

characters.name: Sujangphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sudangphaa; died naturally.

characters.name: Suphakphaa
characters.summary: Son of Sujangphaa; died naturally.

characters.name: Susenphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suphakphaa; reigned about half a century and built a temple at Negheriting.
characters.notes: Catalogued scenes cover a long peace and the Tangshu expedition.

characters.name: Suhenphaa
characters.summary: Son of Susenphaa; speared to death in his palace.
characters.fate: Speared to death in his palace

characters.name: Supimphaa
characters.summary: Son of Suhenphaa; died naturally. A catalogued scene shows him trying his father's killers.

characters.name: Suklenmung (Garhgayan Roja)
characters.summary: Made Garhgaon the capital and drove the Koch army off the north bank in 1546. In his reign Hari, Sankardev's son-in-law, was executed, leading Sankardev to leave the kingdom.
characters.notes: Some chronicles suspected him in his father's murder.

characters.name: Sukhaamphaa (Khora Roja)
characters.summary: Longest-reigning Ahom king (about 51 years). Chilarai's 1563 invasion forced the Treaty of Majuli. The Ekasarana faith took firm root in his reign.
characters.notes: Nicknamed Khora Roja after a limp from an elephant fall.

characters.name: Suramphaa (Jayaditya Singha, Bhoga Roja)
characters.summary: Son of Pratap Singha; deposed in 1644 and later murdered.

characters.name: Sutingphaa (Noriya Roja)
characters.summary: Brother of Suramphaa; deposed by the Burhagohain in 1648 and later murdered.

characters.name: Udayaditya Singha (Sunyatphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Chakradhwaj; renewed the war with the Mughals and ordered Lachit to Saraighat. Deposed and executed.

characters.name: Ramdhwaj Singha (Suklamphaa)
characters.summary: Brother of Udayaditya; poisoned in 1674 during court intrigue.

characters.name: Suhung (Samaguria Roja)
characters.summary: Raised to the throne by Debera Borbarua and deposed after about 21 days.

characters.name: Gobar Roja
characters.label: 1675 (about 24 days)
characters.summary: A puppet king under Debera Borbarua, deposed and executed after about 24 days.
characters.notes: Father of Gadadhar Singha.
characters.fate: Deposed and executed after about 24 days

characters.name: Sujinphaa (Arjun Konwar)
characters.summary: Grandson of Pratap Singha, installed by Atan Burhagohain; deposed and died by suicide.

characters.name: Sudoiphaa (Parvatia Roja)
characters.summary: King during the 1679 conspiracy that led to the murder of Atan Burhagohain; deposed and killed.

characters.name: Sulikphaa (Ratnadhwaj Singha, Lora Roja)
characters.summary: A boy king under Laluk Sola Borphukan; deposed and killed. A rule that claimants must be physically unblemished was introduced in his reign.

characters.name: Rajeswar Singha (Suremphaa)
characters.summary: Fourth son of Rudra Singha. Sheltered Bhagyachandra of Manipur, sent the failed 1765 expedition, and married Kuranganayani in 1768. Much of the governing fell to Kirti Chandra Borbarua.
characters.notes: Died at Dergaon in 1769. Added three underground storeys to the Kareng Ghar (Talatal Ghar).

characters.name: Lakshmi Singha (Sunyeophaa)
characters.summary: Made king by Kirti Chandra Borbarua. The Moamoria rebellion began in 1769 and the rebels captured him; royalists restored him in 1770.
characters.notes: Died 13 December 1780.

characters.name: Gaurinath Singha (Suhitpangphaa)
characters.summary: Became king at about fifteen. Rebels took the capital in 1786; British troops under Captain Welsh restored order in lower Assam in 1792–94 and then left. Died at Jorhat in December 1794.
characters.notes: The infobox gives 1794 as the end; the king list gives 1795.

characters.name: Purandar Singha
characters.summary: Installed as a boy in 1818 by Ruchinath Burhagohain, lost the throne to the Burmese in 1819, and was made a tributary prince by the British in 1833. Deposed in September 1838.
characters.notes: Born 1807, died 1 October 1846 at Jorhat. Also called Suremphaa II.

characters.name: Jogeswar Singha
characters.summary: A puppet king installed by the Burmese commander Mingimaha Tilwa in 1821; removed in 1822.

characters.name: Rajani
characters.label: early 14th century
characters.summary: Daughter of the Kamata king (Kamateswar), given with her sister Bhajani to Sukhaangphaa to seal a truce. Mother of Sukhrangphaa, Sutuphaa, Tyao Khamti and Tyao Chulai.

characters.name: Bhajani
characters.label: early 14th century
characters.summary: Rajani's sister, also given to Sukhaangphaa under the treaty; mother of Chao Pulai.

characters.name: Chao Pulai
characters.label: 14th century
characters.summary: Son of Sukhaangphaa and Bhajani. The project catalogue shows him meeting Kamata envoys and being made governor of Sadiya.
characters.notes: Governor role comes from the catalogue only.

characters.name: Ramani Gabharu
characters.summary: Sent to the Mughal court under the 1663 Treaty of Ghilajharighat. Sources differ on whether she was Jayadhwaj Singha's daughter or Lachit's niece.

characters.name: Pakhori Gabharu
characters.label: 17th century
characters.summary: Daughter of Momai Tamuli Borbarua and sister of Lachit; queen to Ahom kings.

characters.name: Ambika
characters.label: Bar Raja 1732–1739
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Phuleswari's sister. Sponsored the Hastividyarnava and the Sivasagar Siva Doul.
characters.notes: Sources give her death as 1738 or the end of her reign as 1739.

characters.name: Sarbeswari (Endari)
characters.label: Bar Raja 1739–1744
characters.role: Queen who ruled as Bar Raja
characters.summary: Held the same authority as her predecessors but was less active in patronising Shaktism.

characters.name: Kuranganayani
characters.label: married 1768; active to 1770
characters.role: Manipuri princess, queen of the Ahom kingdom
characters.summary: Married Rajeswar Singha in 1768 as thanks for Ahom help to her father. After his death she was taken by the rebel Ragha Moran and helped bring about his killing in April 1770; she later married Lakshmi Singha.

characters.name: Numali Rajmao
characters.label: active 1817–1818
characters.summary: Reportedly behind the plot that led to the murder of Badan Chandra Borphukan.

characters.name: First Burhagohain (Thaomung)
characters.label: c. 1228 (office created by Sukaphaa)
characters.summary: The Burhagohain and Borgohain offices were created by Sukaphaa. The personal names given in the project catalogue are unverified.
characters.notes: Name “Thaomung” comes from the project catalogue only.

characters.name: First Borgohain (Thaomung)
characters.label: c. 1228 (office created by Sukaphaa)
characters.summary: See the first Burhagohain: the personal name is unverified.

characters.name: Khenphung Borgohain
characters.label: c. 1490
characters.summary: An Ahom Borgohain in the project catalogue, ambushed by the Tangshu Nagas.

characters.name: Konseng Barpatragohain
characters.label: office created 1527
characters.summary: Appointed the first Borpatragohain in 1527 by Suhungmung, the year the Ahoms defeated the first Muslim invasion.

characters.name: Ton Kham Borgohain
characters.summary: Defeated Turbak's invasion and pursued the invaders to the Karatoya river.

characters.name: Aikhek Burhagohain
characters.summary: Offered little resistance to Chilarai's 1563 invasion and was removed as Burhagohain after the Treaty of Majuli.

characters.name: Langi Panisiya
characters.label: office created 1615 (catalogue)
characters.summary: First holder of the Borphukan office, based at Kajali, created under Pratap Singha.

characters.name: Manthir Bharali Barua (Parbatia Phukan)
characters.label: mid-17th century
characters.summary: A Kayastha viceroy of western Assam whose appointment caused resentment among Ahom nobles.

characters.name: Laluk Sola Borphukan
characters.label: Borphukan 1672–1677; d. 1680
characters.summary: Elder brother of Lachit; succeeded him as Borphukan. Handed Guwahati to the Mughals in 1679 and was assassinated by his bodyguard in 1680.
characters.notes: Wikipedia dates his tenure 1672–1677 and his death 1680.

characters.name: Debera Borbarua
characters.label: c. 1672–1675
characters.summary: Dominated the court in the 1672–1675 succession struggle, setting up the short-lived kings Suhung and Gobar Roja.
characters.notes: From the project catalogue only; check against the Buranjis.

characters.name: Ghanashyam Khanikar
characters.label: c. 1698–1705
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue as the architect behind Rudra Singha's building of Rangpur.
characters.notes: Not found in the Rudra Singha article; treat as unverified.

characters.name: Krishnaram Bhattacharya Nyayavagish
characters.label: early 18th century
characters.summary: A scholar from Nabadwip invited as religious guide under Rudra Singha; later adviser (Parbatiya Gosain) under Siva Singha.

characters.name: Niranjan Deva (Niranjan Bapu)
characters.label: mid-17th century
characters.summary: Initiated Jayadhwaj Singha and was made head of Auniati Satra.

characters.name: Haranath Bitarual Phukan
characters.summary: Led the 1765 army sent to help Manipur against the Burmese; the jungle route defeated it and it became known as the War of the Creepers.

characters.name: Kirti Chandra Borbarua (Gendhela)
characters.label: active 1751–1769
characters.summary: Held real power under Rajeswar Singha and made Lakshmi Singha king in 1769. Had the Buranjis collected and many destroyed over references to his low origins.

characters.name: Subedar Rup Singh
characters.summary: Killed Badan Chandra Borphukan, in a plot backed by the queen-mother.

characters.name: Ruchinath Burhagohain
characters.label: Burhagohain from 1817
characters.summary: Eldest son of Purnananda; became Burhagohain in 1817, deposed Chandrakanta in February 1818 and installed Purandar Singha, and later sought British help.

characters.name: Aniruddhadeva
characters.summary: Vaishnava teacher who founded the Moamara satra, whose followers later led the Moamoria rebellion.
characters.notes: Dates from memory of standard accounts; verify.

characters.name: Mayamara Mahanta
characters.summary: Intervened to spare Lakshmi Singha's life when the rebels captured him in 1769.

characters.name: Ragha Neog (Raghab Borbarua)
characters.label: d. 11 April 1770
characters.summary: Flogged over elephant levies in September 1769, which sparked the revolt. Became Borbarua and was killed in April 1770 by nobles aided by Kuranganayani.

characters.name: Naharkhora Saikia
characters.label: d. 1770
characters.summary: Co-leader with Ragha; helped install his son Ramakanta as rebel king and was executed in the 1770 purge.

characters.name: Ramakanta
characters.label: Nov 1769 – 1770
characters.summary: Naharkhora's son, placed on the throne by the rebels in November 1769 and executed in 1770.

characters.name: Harihar Tanti
characters.summary: Reorganised the Dafla-Bhatia rebels in 1786 and administered the north bank of the Brahmaputra.

characters.name: Bharat Singha
characters.label: d. 1799
characters.summary: Moamoria chief placed on the throne after the 1785–86 rebel victory; coins were struck in his name. Killed in 1799 (another page gives 1800).

characters.name: Sarbananda Singha
characters.label: to 1805
characters.role: Rebel ruler of the Moran tracts
characters.summary: Ruled the Moran tracts from Bengmara. After fighting royalists in 1805 he accepted peace, became Barsenapati and governed the autonomous Matak kingdom.

characters.name: Krishnanarayan (Darrang)
characters.summary: Rebelled in Darrang in 1791 and occupied North Guwahati with Haradatta; defeated by Captain Welsh in 1792.

characters.name: Gosain Kamal (Kamal Narayan)
characters.label: 16th century
characters.summary: Step-brother of Nara Narayan; built the Gohain Kamal Ali road, governed Brahmapur (Khaspur) and opened the secret road for Chilarai's invasion of 1546.
characters.relation: Son of Biswa Singha; first governor of Khaspur (Brahmapur)

characters.name: Raghudev
characters.summary: Son of Chilarai; claimed the eastern Koch lands at Barnagar in 1581 and stopped paying tribute after Nara Narayan died in 1587, making the division permanent. Father of Parikshit Narayan, Man Singha and Mangaldoi (wife of Pratap Singha).
characters.notes: Defeated a Mughal army in 1597. His daughter Mangaldoi married Pratap Singha in 1603.

characters.name: Lakshmi Narayan
characters.summary: First king of Koch Bihar after the split; submitted to the Mughal subahdar in 1609 and joined the 1612 Mughal attack on Koch Hajo.
characters.notes: Other sources give 1586 for the start and 1627 for his death.

characters.name: Parikshit Narayan
characters.summary: Eldest son of Raghudev. Defeated by Lakshmi Narayan and the Mughals in 1602 and again in 1612; he surrendered at Pandu in 1614 and was taken to Delhi. His brothers Balinarayan and Gaj Narayan fled to the Ahoms.
characters.notes: Another source gives his death as 1616. The Koch Hajo article lists his reign as 1603–1613 but describes events in 1614.

characters.name: Balinarayan (Dharma Narayan)
characters.summary: Fled to the Ahoms in 1613; Pratap Singha made him tributary king of Darrang (between the Barnadi and Bharali) after the 1615 victory. Fought beside the Ahoms for two decades and was killed at Singri in 1638.
characters.notes: The article's infobox gives 1638 (1639).
characters.relation: Son of Raghudev; brother of Parikshit

characters.name: Indranarayan
characters.label: c. 1350–1365 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: Kamata king weakened by Sikandar Shah's 1357–62 invasion; some historians say he and Mahamanikya resisted Sikandar Shah around 1362. A Bhuyan then took power.
characters.notes: Dated 1350–1365 in two lists; 1350–1385 in another.

characters.name: Arimatta (Sasanka)
characters.label: c. 1365–1385 (reconstructed)
characters.summary: A Bhuyan of Darrang who killed Indranarayan and took the Kamata throne.
characters.notes: It is not known when Baro-Bhuyan rule began. Gajanka, Sukranka and Mriganka are listed as successors without dates.

characters.name: Mriganka (Jungal Balahu)
characters.label: c. 1385–1440 (undated successor)
characters.summary: Removed by the Khen dynasty.
characters.notes: Also called Jungal Balahu; removed by Niladhwaj of the Khen dynasty.

characters.name: Niladhwaj
characters.summary: Founder of the Khen dynasty, ruling from Kamatapur (now Gosanimari) after Mriganka. An 18th-century source calls him Kanta Nath, of humble origin.
characters.notes: Origins disputed: a local from Jambari or a migrant from Tripura, per different accounts. The page is a stub.

characters.name: Chakradhwaj (Khen)
characters.summary: Son of Niladhwaj and second Khen ruler; his son Nilambar succeeded him.

characters.name: Nilambar
characters.summary: Last Khen king, the most powerful of his line. Expanded Kamata into Kamrup, Darrang, northern Mymensingh and parts of Cooch Behar and built roads; Husain Shah's army took Kamatapur after a long siege in 1498.
characters.notes: Tradition says the minister Sachipatra urged the invasion after Nilambar executed his son.

characters.name: Alauddin Husain Shah
characters.label: r. 1493–1519
characters.summary: Sultan of Bengal; his general Shah Ismail Ghazi took Kamatapur in 1498–99 and annexed the land up to Hajo by 1502. His son Danyal governed it until the Bhuyans overran the garrison.
characters.notes: Sources give 1493 or 1494 as the start of his reign and 1518 or 1519 as the end.

characters.name: Satyanarayana (Ratnanarayana)
characters.label: late 14th century (grant of 1392)
characters.summary: Son of Nandi; ruled from Sadhayapura. A later Chutia king names Ratnanarayana, identified with him, as king of Kamatapura, which may show a link between Sadiya and Kamata.
characters.notes: The Ratnanarayana identification is a scholarly suggestion.

characters.name: Lakshminarayana (Dharmanarayana)
characters.label: early 15th century
characters.summary: Chutia king known from sources dated 1392 and 1401.

characters.name: Durlabhnarayana (Chutia)
characters.label: early 15th century (grant of 1428)
characters.summary: Chutia king known from a grant dated 1428.
characters.notes: Not the Kamata king of the same name.

characters.name: Muktadharmanarayana
characters.label: mid-15th century
characters.summary: Known from an inscription dated 1442.

characters.name: Dhirnarayan
characters.label: to 1523–24
characters.summary: Built a fort at Dikhowmukh in 1513, was routed attacking the Ahom fort at Dibru in 1523, and was killed, ending the kingdom in 1523–24.
characters.notes: Known from an inscription dated 1522.

characters.name: Khorapha
characters.label: c. 1520–1526
characters.summary: Issued a silver coin in 1520 and was killed in an Ahom attack in 1526.

characters.name: Khunkhara
characters.summary: Succeeded his brother Khorapha and fled Dimapur when the Ahoms attacked in 1531.

characters.name: Detsung (Dersung)
characters.summary: Installed by Suhungmung, to whom he gave his sister in marriage; killed when he tried to break free. The Ahoms occupied Dimapur in 1536.

characters.name: Yasho Narayan (Satrudaman)
characters.label: c. 1583–1601
characters.summary: Ruled North Cachar, the Dhansiri valley and parts of Sylhet and struck coins in his name.

characters.name: Tamradhwaj Narayan
characters.summary: Declared independence; Rudra Singha invaded Maibong in December 1706 and destroyed its fort. Tamradhwaj fled to Jaintia and was imprisoned.

characters.name: Krishnachandra Narayan
characters.summary: Sheltered Moamoria rebels, causing Ahom–Dimasa skirmishes from 1803 to 1805; helped Manipur against the Burmese.

characters.name: Govindachandra Narayan
characters.summary: Restored by the British after the 1826 Treaty of Yandabo; died in 1830.
characters.notes: The two sources split his reign into two periods.

characters.name: Jasa Manik
characters.summary: Jaintia king whose manoeuvres are linked to the Dimasa–Ahom conflict of 1618.

characters.name: Ram Singh I (Jaintia)
characters.summary: Kidnapped the Dimasa king, prompting Rudra Singha's 1707–08 invasion; died an Ahom captive.

characters.name: Ram Singh II (Jaintia)
characters.summary: Long-reigning Jaintia king who agreed in 1824 to deal only with the British.

characters.name: Bhagyachandra (Jai Singh)
characters.summary: Fled to Ahom territory after the Burmese invasion of 1764 and was sheltered by Rajeswar Singha, who backed his return; reinstated in 1773. Promoted Vaishnavism and the Manipuri Raas Leela.

characters.name: Gambhir Singha
characters.summary: Repulsed the Burmese in 1825.

characters.name: Hema Saraswati
characters.label: 13th–14th century (uncertain)
characters.summary: Counted among the first known Assamese writers, patron Durlabhnarayan. His Prahlada Charita is regarded as the earliest known Assamese poem.
characters.notes: No explicit dates in the source.

characters.name: Harihara Vipra
characters.label: 14th century
characters.summary: Pre-Vaishnava Assamese poet; wrote Babruvahanar Yuddha.
characters.notes: Century from a category tag only.

characters.name: Madhava Kandali
characters.label: 14th century
characters.summary: Author of the Saptakanda Ramayana, regarded as the oldest rendering of the Ramayana into an Indo-Aryan language. Patron: Mahamanikya, a Kachari king.
characters.notes: Dated by a stone inscription equated with 1352.

characters.name: Damodardev
characters.label: 1488–1598 (traditional)
characters.summary: Disciple of Sankardev and founder of the Brahma Sanghati tradition.
characters.notes: Dates from standard accounts; not checked against a page.

characters.name: Hari (Sankardev's son-in-law)
characters.label: mid-16th century
characters.summary: Captured and executed in Suklenmung's reign, which led Sankardev to leave the Ahom kingdom (some chronicles place it under Suhungmung).

characters.name: Ananta Kandali
characters.summary: Poet from Hajo, born Haricharan; wrote Kumara Harana.

characters.name: Bhattadev
characters.summary: Prose translator of the Bhagavata and Gita (Katha Bhagavata, Katha Gita); head of Patbausi satra and founder of Byaskuchi satra.

characters.name: Bit Malik
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue as leading the first Muslim invasion that Suhungmung defeated in 1527.

characters.name: Turbak
characters.label: d. 1533
characters.summary: Led the 1532–33 invasion, defeating Suklen at Singri before the Ahoms counterattacked; killed near the Bharali river.
characters.notes: Sources disagree on his origin (Turko-Afghan or Bengali).

characters.name: Allah Yar Khan
characters.summary: Signed the Treaty of Asurar Ali with Momai Tamuli in 1639, fixing the border on the Brahmaputra.

characters.name: Aurangzeb
characters.label: ordered the 1667 expedition
characters.summary: Ordered Ram Singh's 1667 counter-expedition against the Ahoms.

characters.name: Ram Singh I of Amber
characters.summary: Led the 1667–1671 Mughal invasion of Assam; defeated at Saraighat in 1671 and demoted on his return.

characters.name: Dilir Khan
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue among the Mughal commanders of Mir Jumla's 1662 invasion.
characters.notes: Not found in the Wikipedia articles consulted.

characters.name: Syed Firoz Khan
characters.label: c. 1663–1667
characters.summary: Captured by the Ahoms and later released; carried Ram Singh's demands to the Ahom court.

characters.name: Shihabuddin Talish
characters.label: chronicler of 1662
characters.summary: Chronicler of Mir Jumla's invasion of Assam.
characters.notes: Role from the project catalogue.

characters.name: Munawar Khan
characters.summary: Named among the Mughal commanders at Saraighat.

characters.name: Muhammad Azam Shah
characters.summary: Invited in 1679 to take the Saraighat fort after Laluk Sola's surrender.

characters.name: Raja Satrajit of Bhusna
characters.summary: Co-led the 1615 imperial army with Abu Bakr and stirred up Balinarayan's invasion of Kamrup.

characters.name: Abu Bakr
characters.summary: Co-led the 1615 imperial army that began the first Mughal attack on Assam.

characters.name: Qasim Khan Chishti
characters.label: c. 1615
characters.summary: His mistreatment of hill chiefs of Dhanikal led to the Ahom asylum dispute.

characters.name: Captain Thomas Welsh
characters.summary: Led the British contingent that took Guwahati in 1792 and Rangpur in March 1794; recalled in April 1794.

characters.name: Lord Cornwallis
characters.summary: Ordered the dispatch of Captain Welsh's troops to Assam.

characters.name: Bodawpaya
characters.label: king of Burma 1782–1819
characters.summary: Received Badan Chandra Borphukan in 1816 and sent the first Burmese expedition into Assam in 1817.

characters.name: Kiamingi (Ala Mingi)
characters.summary: Commanded Bodawpaya's second invasion in 1819; after the Burmese victory he reinstalled Chandrakanta Singha.

characters.name: Mingimaha Tilwa
characters.summary: Sent to Assam in 1821; installed Jogeswar Singha, defeated Chandrakanta in June 1822 and was declared Raja of Assam, ending Ahom rule.

characters.name: Maha Bandula
characters.label: d. 1 April 1825
characters.summary: Led 20,000 men to defeat Chandrakanta in 1822; killed at Danubyu in the First Anglo-Burmese War.

characters.name: Bagyidaw
characters.label: king of Burma 1819–1837
characters.summary: Sent Mingimaha Tilwa to Assam in 1821 and ruled through the First Anglo-Burmese War.

characters.name: David Scott
characters.label: active 1823–1826
characters.role: British Agent on the north-east frontier
characters.summary: British official in Assam and the north-east in the years before and after Yandabo.
characters.notes: Role from general knowledge; check against a dedicated source.

characters.name: Colonel Alfred Richards
characters.summary: Named in the project catalogue in the First Anglo-Burmese War scenes.

characters.name: Sir Archibald Campbell
characters.summary: Led the 1824 Yangon expedition and co-signed the Treaty of Yandabo on 24 February 1826.

characters.name: Badaucha (Moran chief)
characters.label: c. 1235
characters.summary: A Moran chief whose daughter Sukaphaa married as part of the Ahom settlement of the Brahmaputra valley.
characters.notes: The project catalogue spells the name Bodousa.

characters.name: Thakumatha (Barahi chief)
characters.label: c. 1235
characters.summary: A Barahi chief whose daughter Sukaphaa married as part of the Ahom settlement of the Brahmaputra valley.
characters.notes: The project catalogue spells the name Thakumtha.

characters.name: Thomas Campbell Robertson
characters.summary: His 1833 report recommended Purandar Singha, whose disposition he called mild and pacific, as the British choice for tributary prince of Upper Assam.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off; included because it ends the Purandar Singha story.

characters.name: Captain Francis Jenkins
characters.role: British Commissioner and Agent to the Governor-General
characters.summary: Investigated Purandar Singha's administration in 1835–38 and reported it as a hotbed of corruption; Purandar was deposed and the territory annexed in September 1838.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off; included because it ends the Purandar Singha story.

characters.name: Samudrapala
characters.label: c. 1100 (no dates given)
characters.summary: Listed as ruling Kamarupa proper after Jayapala; no dates or events are given.

characters.name: Ramapala (Pala Empire of Bengal)
characters.label: c. 1072–1126 (sources vary)
characters.summary: Conquered western Kamarupa and installed Timgyadeva as governor. Sources differ on whether he took only parts of north Bengal or Kamarupa itself.
characters.notes: Reign given as 1072–1126 or 1077–1133.

characters.name: Timgyadeva
characters.label: c. 1110–1126
characters.role: Governor and ruler of western Kamarupa
characters.summary: Made governor of Kamarupa by Ramapala, ruling from Hamshkonchi; later rebelled and ruled independently until he was replaced.
characters.notes: The claim that he threw off Pala rule is marked as needing a citation.

characters.name: Kumarapala (Pala king of Bengal)
characters.label: early 12th century
characters.summary: Sent Vaidyadeva to put down Timgyadeva's rebellion in Kamarupa and kept friendly relations with him.
characters.notes: Some accounts call him Timgyadeva's son, which looks like a mistake; he is Ramapala's son.

characters.name: Vaidyadeva
characters.label: c. 1126–1140
characters.summary: Replaced Timgyadeva under Kumarapala, then in effect created a separate kingdom after Kumarapala's death. Issued grants in the old Kamarupa style under the elephant seal and took the title Maharajadhiraja.
characters.notes: The Kamauli plates date his fourth year while governing under Kumarapala.

characters.name: Bhaskara (lunar dynasty)
characters.label: c. 1120–1200 (dynasty)
characters.summary: First of a “lunar dynasty” known from one 1185 inscription; held parts of Kamrup, Darrang and Sonitpur on the north bank.
characters.notes: No individual dates; the four rulers share the span 1120–1200.

characters.name: Rayarideva
characters.label: 12th century
characters.summary: Member of the lunar dynasty of the north bank, known only from the 1185 inscription.

characters.name: Udayakarna
characters.label: 12th century (inscription 1185)
characters.summary: Member of the lunar dynasty known from the 1185 inscription.

characters.name: Vallabhadeva
characters.label: late 12th century

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Iwaz Khalji
characters.summary: Invaded Kamarupa in 1226–27, was worsted near Nagaon and withdrew to Lakhnauti, where he was captured and killed in 1227–28 by Nasiruddin Mahmud.

characters.name: Nasiruddin Mahmud
characters.summary: Son of Iltutmish; took Bengal after Iwaz Khalji, entered Kamarupa and installed a tributary king who lost control after Nasiruddin's death in 1229.

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Bahadur Shah
characters.label: raid 1321–1322; d. 1327–28
characters.summary: Raided Kamata as far as Nagaon, meeting ineffective resistance from Pratapdhwaj and the Kacharis, but kept no territory. Killed by Muhammad Tughlaq in 1327–28.

characters.name: Shamsuddin Ilyas Shah
characters.label: d. c. November 1357
characters.summary: His forces advanced up the Brahmaputra and occupied Kamrup, including Guwahati, before his death around November 1357.

characters.name: Sikandar Shah of Bengal
characters.label: expeditions 1357–1362
characters.summary: Advanced to the Kopili river, where Kamata, Bhuyan and Barahi forces fought him near Gachtal. Silver coins of 1360 carry a Kamrup mint name, but how long he held it is unclear.
characters.notes: The outcome of the Gachtal fighting is not stated in the article.

characters.name: Ghiyasuddin Azam Shah
characters.label: c. 1396–1400 (reign 1389–1410)
characters.summary: An inscription at Boko in Kamrup shows the Sultanate held the region for some years. The Kamata king, allied with the Ahoms by marriage, drove him back across the Karatoya.
characters.notes: Dates are inferred from coins.

characters.name: Shamsuddin Muzaffar Shah
characters.summary: Invaded Kamata and took parts of it, issuing coins with the title Kamata Mardan, before Husain Shah.

characters.name: Shah Ismail Ghazi
characters.summary: Led about 24,000 men and a river flotilla to besiege and destroy Kamatapur and capture Nilambar.

characters.name: Shahzada Danyal
characters.label: c. 1502–c. 1510
characters.role: Governor of the conquered Kamata region
characters.summary: Husain Shah's son, made governor of the territory up to Hajo; the Bhuyans under Harup Narayan overran his garrison and ended Sultanate rule within about ten years.

characters.name: Sachipatra
characters.label: 1498 (traditional)
characters.summary: In the traditional account, a minister whose son Nilambar executed for an affair with the queen; said to have urged Husain Shah to invade. Escaped and was never heard of again.
characters.notes: Traditional, not independently documented.

characters.name: Candivara (Chandibar)
characters.label: 14th century
characters.summary: Said to have been a former ruler of Kannauj who fled north India; Durlabhnarayan of Kamata settled his group at Langamaguri and later Bordowa. A descendant was Srimanta Sankardev.
characters.notes: Possibly fled after the 1353 campaign against Ilyas Shah.

characters.name: Rajadhara
characters.label: 14th–15th century
characters.summary: Son of Candivara; captured by the Bhutiyas, later freed, and succeeded his father as leader of the Baro-Bhuyans.

characters.name: Harup Narayan
characters.label: c. 1500–1515
characters.role: Bhuyan leader and Chota Raja of Bausi
characters.summary: Leader of the Assamese Bhuyans who overran Danyal's garrison and ended Sultanate rule about ten years after 1498, before the Koch rose.
characters.notes: The article gives no exact dates.

characters.name: Gandharva Raya
characters.label: 15th century (ancestor of Harup Narayan)
characters.summary: Ancestor of Harup Narayan in the second group of Bhuyans.

characters.name: Gajanka
characters.label: late 14th–15th century (undated)
characters.summary: Listed as a successor of Arimatta; no dates are given.

characters.name: Sukranka
characters.label: 15th century (undated)
characters.summary: Listed as a successor of Arimatta; no dates are given.

characters.name: Mahamanikya (Barahi king)
characters.label: c. 1330–1370
characters.role: Barahi (Kachari) king of the Kapili valley
characters.summary: Ruled around Nagaon, Morigaon and Hojai; patron of the poet Madhava Kandali. A Hojai (Lanka) inscription dated 1352 records a land grant; some historians say he joined Kamata and the Bhuyans against Sikandar Shah around 1362.
characters.notes: Called Borahi-Kachari king Manikpha in one source; the lineage label varies.

characters.name: Bhopal (Kachari, traditional list)
characters.label: 1286–1316 (traditional list)
characters.summary: Named in a popular king list as a Kachari ruler of the 13th–14th century; not found in the scholarly sources reviewed.
characters.notes: Treat as unverified.

characters.name: Purandar (Kachari, traditional list)
characters.label: 1316–1336 (traditional list)
characters.summary: Named in the same popular king list; unverified.
characters.notes: Not the Ahom king Purandar Singha.

characters.name: Bicharpatiha (Prakash, traditional list)
characters.label: 1336–1386 (traditional list)
characters.summary: The same list places him at Dimapur from 1336; the Dimasa Kingdom article says early king lists are late constructions and should be treated with caution.
characters.notes: Treat as unverified.

characters.name: Nandi (Nandisvara)
characters.label: second half of the 14th century
characters.summary: Ruled from Sadhayapura (Sadiya); known from a grant issued by his son Satyanarayana, who also names his mother Daivaki.

characters.name: Pratyaksanarayana (Yasanarayana)
characters.label: mid-15th century
characters.summary: Chutia king known without dates; the page notes a possible match with Yasanarayana of the Dhenukhana plate.

characters.name: Yasamanarayana
characters.label: late 15th century
characters.summary: Chutia king of the late 15th century; may be the Yasanarayana of the Dhenukhana plate.

characters.name: Purandarnarayana
characters.label: late 15th century
characters.summary: Chutia king listed before Dhirnarayan; no events are given.

characters.name: Birpal (legendary)
characters.label: legend
characters.summary: Figure of the Chutiyar Rajar Vamsavali (published 1850), a late manuscript that scholars treat as legendary; historians think it was composed in the early 19th century.
characters.notes: No historical standing; included because it appears in popular lists.

characters.name: Kasitora
characters.summary: A minister said to have been defeated alongside Dhirnarayan.

characters.name: Sadhaknarayan
characters.summary: Prince after the fall; accounts differ on whether he was deported to Darrang or killed.

characters.name: Phrasengmung Borgohain
characters.label: from 1524
characters.summary: Appointed by Suhungmung to govern Sadiya after the Chutia kingdom was annexed.

characters.name: Chaothai Khum Burhagohain
characters.summary: Brought the young Sudangphaa to Charaideo and enthroned him in 1397.

characters.name: Thao Cheoken
characters.summary: The trader who found the young prince Sudangphaa in Habung.

characters.name: Tai Sulai
characters.label: c. 1400
characters.summary: A rival claimant to the Ahom throne who fled to Mungkang and gained an invasion force; Sudangphaa defeated it and the 1401 treaty fixed the Patkai boundary.

characters.name: Nangchukham Borgohain
characters.summary: Sudangphaa's commander who pursued the Mungkang invaders.

characters.name: Tasim Pou Borgohain
characters.label: c. 1400
characters.summary: Minister who led the Mungkang invasion force for the claimant Tai Sulai.

characters.name: Hajo (Koch chief)
characters.label: 15th century
characters.summary: Father of Hira, so maternal grandfather of Biswa Singha; a chief of Koch Hajo's ancestral line.
characters.notes: Reign not given.

characters.name: Hariya Mandal (Hari Das)
characters.label: late 15th century
characters.role: Mech chief, father of Biswa Singha
characters.summary: Husband of Hira and father of Biswa Singha; a Mech (Bodo) chief.

characters.name: Sisu (Sisya Singha)
characters.label: 16th century
characters.summary: Brother of Biswa Singha, made yuvaraj; his descendants became the Raikut kings of Jalpaiguri.

characters.name: Man Singha (Koch Hajo prince)
characters.label: c. 1600
characters.summary: Son of Raghudev and brother of Parikshit Narayan.

characters.name: Mangaldoi (Mangaldahi)
characters.label: married 1603–1608
characters.role: Koch princess, wife of Pratap Singha
characters.summary: Daughter of Raghudev (or Parikshit Narayan in another source); married Pratap Singha to secure the alliance with Koch Hajo.

characters.name: Bir Narayan
characters.summary: Pleasure-loving ruler per the Cooch Behar State article.
characters.notes: The district history page gives his death as 1632; another list gives 1627–32.

characters.name: Pran (Prana) Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned almost four decades, one of the longest Koch Bihar reigns before the 18th century.
characters.notes: The district page says he reigned till 1666.

characters.name: Moda (Madan) Narayan
characters.summary: His officers killed Chandra Narayan around 1667; he died in 1680 without a male heir.

characters.name: Basudev Narayan
characters.summary: Killed in 1682 in a skirmish with his kinsman Jagna Narayan.

characters.name: Mahendra Narayan (Koch Bihar)
characters.summary: A minor king, great-grandson of Pran Narayan according to the district page.
characters.notes: Not the Darrang king of the same name.

characters.name: Rup Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned 21 years.

characters.name: Upendra Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned nearly half a century; succeeded by his young son.

characters.name: Devendra Narayan
characters.summary: Installed as a boy under the guardianship of the Nazir Deo, Lalit Narayan; died in August 1765.

characters.name: Dhairjendra (Dhairyendra) Narayan
characters.summary: First reign under the Bhutanese ambassador Pensuthma; deposed in 1770 and abdicated after the 1774 peace between the British and Bhutan, returning in 1775.

characters.name: Rajendra Narayan (1770–1772)
characters.summary: Placed on the throne by Bhutan with Pensuthma as regent.

characters.name: Dharendra Narayan
characters.summary: Two short reigns. After the British captured the capital in 1772 and the 1774 peace with Bhutan, Dhairjendra abdicated in his favour.

characters.name: Bijendra Narayan
characters.summary: Reigned between Dharendra Narayan's two terms.

characters.name: Harendra Narayan
characters.summary: Ruled for over fifty years, under regents until 1801. His reign spans the 1826 end of Ahom rule.

characters.name: Shivendra Narayan
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Narendra Narayan
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Nripendra Narayan
characters.summary: Ruled 1863–1911; regents until 1883.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Raj Rajendra Narayan II
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Jitendra Narayan
characters.summary: Ruled 1913–1922; father of Gayatri Devi.
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Jagaddipendra Narayan
characters.summary: Ruled 1922–1949 (the biography section gives 1970 as the end).
characters.notes: After the 1826 cut-off of the main research; included to complete the Koch Bihar line.

characters.name: Mahendra Narayan (Darrang)
characters.label: after 1638 (no dates)
characters.summary: Listed as Balinarayan's successor (a son, per some accounts); no dates are given.
characters.notes: Sources conflict on the order of succession.

characters.name: Chandra Narayan (Darrang)
characters.label: 17th century (no dates)
characters.summary: Son of Mahendra Narayan; installed as tributary ruler after Koch princes helped the Ahoms drive out the Mughals.

characters.name: Surya Narayan (Darrang)
characters.label: to 1682
characters.summary: Captured by the Mughal commander Mansur Khan in 1682, who installed his five-year-old brother; the Ahoms removed the Mughals later that year.

characters.name: Indra Narayan (Darrang)
characters.label: after 1682 (no dates)
characters.summary: A Darrang ruler installed by the Ahoms, listed after Surya Narayan in one genealogy.

characters.name: Hangsanarayan (Darrang)
characters.label: to c. 1789
characters.summary: Executed by royal troops around the time of the Moamoria troubles; father of the rebel prince Krishnanarayan.

characters.label: founded c. 1613–1671
characters.summary: Son of Parikshit Narayan; the Mughals made him zamindar between the Sankosh and Manas rivers. Bijni's control is dated 1671–1864.

characters.summary: Brother of Parikshit Narayan and Balinarayan; set up as tributary ruler of Beltola in 1615 under the Ahom Borphukan.
characters.notes: Beltola reign years are given only for a few rulers in the source.

characters.summary: Son of Gaj Narayan.

characters.label: fought at Saraighat 1671
characters.summary: Son of Shivendra; fought with the Ahoms under Lachit Borphukan at Saraighat and was then installed as king of Beltola.
characters.notes: Beltola reign years are given only for a few rulers in the source.

characters.label: signed with the East India Company, Oct 1826
characters.summary: Son of Jay Narayan; signed an ordinance with the East India Company in October 1826 acknowledging its overlordship; married a Manipuri princess.
characters.notes: Beltola reign years are given only for a few rulers in the source.

characters.notes: Beltola reign years are given only for a few rulers in the source.
